newsitem.title: UK: Oil production costs to inevitably fall - Shell exec.
newsitem.headline: Oil production costs to inevitably fall - Shell exec.

text.p: Oil and gas production costs will inevitably continue to decline, postponing further the day when OPEC's big Middle East producers can hold sway over the rest of the world's suppliers, a senior Shell executive said on Monday.
"We have continually underestimated non-OPEC production," said Mark Moody-Stuart, group managing director of Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
"I think we know there will be an absolute continuing cost-cutting drive. It's just like gravity or breathing," he told an oil conference in London.
"You wonder whether producer power will ever switch back to the three big Middle East producers (Saudi Arabia, Iran and Kuwait)."
Technical costs for the same oilfields had fallen about 50 cents a barrel per year since 1986, giving a huge boost to commercially exploitable reserves.

Moody-Stuart said that if world demand growth proved low and non-OPEC supply kept rising, there might be no room for OPEC to produce more crude for some time to come, possibly as far as the year 2020.

Statoil's executive vice president Johan Nic Vold said his company was aiming to cut costs on new developments by 40 to 50 percent by nurturing alliances with supply contractors and other service areas of the industry.
"We as an industry are likely to find ourselves in an alliance networked landscape," he said.
Both men were speaking at the 17th Oil and Money conference sponsored by the International Herald Tribune and the Oil Daily/PIW publications. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4984
